messages:
maya: customer (acme-inc) reports streaming connection abruptly resets mid-response. client sees connection reset, our gateway logs econnreset and we billed as 5xx. attached sample trace and curl. Can SRE reproduce?

sam: looking. can you paste request id + trace link?

maya: req_id: r-62f9b1d1, trace: https://redwood-traces/acme/r-62f9b1d1

eli: quick glance — gateway saw FIN? logs show socket read error EPIPE after sending chunked trailer. paste of gateway log:
```
[2024-02-12T16:12:11Z] conn=12 write=2048 err=EPIPE write_error=write: broken pipe
[2024-02-12T16:12:11Z] upstream: client reset by peer (RST)
```

julia: customer says extension closes tab mid-stream. that sends RST in some browsers. historically we treat any RST as 5xx for billing. that's causing disputes.

maya: repro steps I used:
```
# python quick repro
import socket, time
s=socket.create_connection(('gateway.redwood.ai', 443))
# TLS + http handshake omitted for brevity
# write headers + first chunk
s.send(b'POST /v1/stream HTTP/1.1\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n...\r\n\r\n')
s.send(b'5\r\nhello\r\n0\r\n\r\n')
# close socket abruptly
s.shutdown(socket.SHUT_RDWR)
s.close()
```

eli: that's great repro. root cause likely our metric: any abnormal socket teardown during active stream increments 5xx counter. we need to disambiguate client-initiated RST vs server-side error. propose heuristics: if client RST occurs within X seconds of last chunk and no upstream error, mark as client-abort. Also capture FIN vs RST from kernel if possible.

sam: ops-bot shows no infra alerts. can we add a non-billing label for these events while we triage?

ops-bot: incident labelled: streaming-client-abort-investigation, owners: @eli @sam, severity: low

maya: filed support ticket to customer to pause billing until we resolve. assigning to eng and SRE.

eli: will follow up with a PR to change counting behavior and a short runbook for support. will post link when ready.

maya: thanks — ping me when PR merged and we'll notify customer. :thumbsup:
